idea-plugin.name: Go MCP++
idea-plugin.description:
Your agent stops grepping Go and starts asking the compiler. 24 tools that answer questions about Go code the way the IDE answers them — through the type system, rather than through text search — added to the MCP server built into GoLand.

GoLand already exposes file reading, text search and patching over MCP. What it does not expose is the Go type system. Go has no implements keyword, so which types satisfy an interface is recorded nowhere in the source — that answer exists only inside the IDE, and no amount of grepping recovers it.

  • Interfaces — who implements one, which ones a type satisfies, and why a type does not. Including the two cases that are invisible to search: a type that declares no method at all and gains the whole set by embedding, and the pointer-receiver trap, where *T satisfies and T does not.
  • Understanding code — resolve a symbol, read its doc and source, list a package's API with struct tags, find usages classified as call, read or write.
  • Changing code — change a signature and every call site with it, safe-delete, inline, move files between packages, fix imports. Every change lands on the IDE's undo stack.
  • Generating — interface stubs, an interface extracted from a type, Go structs from a JSON sample, table-driven test scaffolding.
  • Toolchain — run tests, builds, vet and module commands, returning structured failures rather than a log to re-read.

Requires the bundled MCP Server and Go plugins, and an agent connected to the IDE. Settings | Tools | MCP Server configures that for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others.

Nothing is transmitted anywhere. Usage counters under Settings | Tools | Go MCP++ are held in memory for the session only.

Documentation and agent skills for Claude Code and Codex
